dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: I'll think about my research topic before Nayab finds a new counter card.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About your research topic...

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: I come from a family of academics. Everyone has either worked at the Akademiya or continued their studies there. So, research has become an essential part of my life.

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: I'm from Vahum{RUBY#[S]Aetiology}ana, and am currently conducting research on the history of the desert and King Deshret.

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: One of my younger sisters also happens to be researching the semantics of the ancient King Deshret runes, so occasionally we'll discuss our findings together.

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: But she has to instruct new students during the day, so we can only talk at night.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About that countermeasure card...

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: Well, you know the popular card game "Genius Invokation TCG"? It was invented in Sumeru and then spread throughout Teyvat via Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: I'd only heard about this game before, but never tried it. Then one day, I came here to have a coffee and Nayab invited me to play a round.

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: I was scared out of my wits at first. I thought I'd inadvertently let slip some forbidden knowledge about King Deshret and that the matra had found me.

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: But it was fine in the end. After this matra came over, it was just a few bizarre deck questions from there.

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: That isn't the sort of thing I'm good at. I just ask the questions. As for the solutions, I let him work them out for himself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: See you later. I'm going to order another cup of coffee and think over the problem.

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: Are you sure you've found the correct semantic field for these ancient runes?

dialogues.speaker: Hawa
dialogues.text: Of course I'm not sure. I'm only speculating.

dialogues.speaker: Hawa
dialogues.text: Besides, I discovered that there are overlapping marks on the ancient runes on this stone wall.

dialogues.speaker: Hawa
dialogues.text: So, I have reason to suspect that they may have been carved by people over several generations.

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: Well, that complicates things... In my history researches, the meanings of runes like these can differ significantly from era to era.

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: When will Father finish his desert expedition again? We should ask him what he thinks when he gets back.

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: Or ask Rifaet. Maybe he has some leads.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's pretty hard.

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: Tell me about it. By the time he comes up with a solution, my sisters and I might have already finished our researches.

dialogues.speaker: Iris
dialogues.text: However, doing research is similar to playing cards. You need to think out of the box to make a breakthrough.
